narration.full_text: Let's test your knowledge on real numbers and their properties! Question one: Which of the following numbers is irrational? [pause 3 seconds] The answer is the square root of seven. Question two: The decimal expansion of thirteen divided by forty is what? [pause 3 seconds] It is terminating. Question three: Which of these has a terminating decimal expansion? [pause 3 seconds] The answer is thirteen divided by one hundred twenty-five. Question four: If the HCF is twelve, the LCM is one hundred eighty, and one number is thirty-six, what is the other number? [pause 3 seconds] The other number is sixty. Question five: State the Fundamental Theorem of Arithmetic. [pause 3 seconds] Every integer greater than one is either a prime or can be expressed as a unique product of prime numbers. Question six: Is the square root of thirty-six rational? Justify your answer. [pause 3 seconds] Yes, because the square root of thirty-six is six, which can be written as six over one. Question seven: Write the prime factorization of ninety. [pause 3 seconds] Ninety equals two times three squared times five. Question eight: Find the HCF and LCM of twenty-four and sixty. [pause 3 seconds] The HCF is twelve, and the LCM is one hundred twenty. Question nine: Determine whether seven divided by one hundred twenty-five has a terminating decimal expansion. [pause 3 seconds] Yes, because the denominator's prime factors only include five. Question ten: Express two hundred fifty-two as a product of prime factors. [pause 3 seconds] Two hundred fifty-two equals two squared times three squared times seven. Question eleven: Can the product of two irrational numbers be rational? [pause 3 seconds] Yes, for example, the square root of two multiplied by the square root of two equals two. Great job testing your understanding of these concepts!
